headline: Google has opened a public site that checks whether images, videos or audio were made by AI.
score_reason: Pool 6, lowered 1: the launch was on 6 Oct, before 7 Oct (stale).
importance_line: What changed: anyone can now check AI-made images, videos and audio, which helps people and newsrooms spot fakes; the doubt is that the tool depends on Google's SynthID watermark, and TechCrunch says Microsoft and Meta's own tools are not infallible.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Google launched on Tuesday 6 October a site that lets anyone check whether an image, video or audio clip was made with AI, using its SynthID watermark system. The new part is open access, after the tool had been limited to selected journalists, media professionals and researchers, and Google says people already make about one million checks a day.
notes: Full article read. Google's own launch, so CONFIRMED. Score lowered for the stale rule (event 6 Oct). Still at the report cutoff of 5.
